On each turn, each player exploits the dice results obtained by the active player for their own purposes, in order to enhance the appeal of their speakeasy. The aim of the game is to attract enough customers to reach 12 prestige points. When a player achieves this, the game ends and the player with the highest score wins. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Game Round 3 End of Game 4 Scoring Objective Validate Clients by fulfilling their needs (as rolled by the dice) to get them to come into your speakeasy. Collect enough Clients to earn 12 prestige points and be the winner. Each player starts with one speakeasy card and two Client cards. They begin by placing one Moon token on an available empty Moon token space on their speakeasy card or one of their Clients. Game Round Roll the Dice : The active player rolls 3 white dice (and also the blue and/or orange die if they have unlocked those bonuses). For each arrow icon in their speakeasy, they may reroll one or more dice. Gain Moon Tokens : If any Moon tokens were rolled on the blue or orange die, players with access to that die may gain a corresponding Moon token and immediately place it. If this unlocks a bonus die rolled by the active player, you can now benefit from it. Bonuses need all their spaces covered to unlock the bonus. Action: : All players must simultaneously perform 1 of the following actions: Validate a Client card (if possible) - You must have the required resources on the dice and/or bonuses and be able to discard as many Moon tokens listed on the Client card. After the Client is validated, draw cards to replace them. You can only validate one Client per turn. Take a Moon Token : Take one Moon token and place it on the bonus of your choice. Draw Cards - Draw cards and replace one of your Client cards. This is helpful if you have a Client card that is too difficult to complete. End of Game At the end of a round, if one or more players reach 12 points, the game ends and the player with the most points wins. On a tie, the player with the most Moon tokens left wins. If still tied, the player with the most validated Client cards wins. Scoring This icon gives you 1 point per validated card of the color you have the most. Example: If you have validated 2 green cards and 3 purple cards, this icon gives you 3 points. Warning: If you validate a second card with this icon, count the cards of your second majority color. If you validate a third card with this icon, count the cards of your third majority color, etc. In Advance Mode, you can't score your starting speakeasy color cards for the majority scorings (question-symbol icons). [Rating: 3/10] Nothing about this felt like I was making interesting decisions. The race element is fine and it has Splendor meets Yahtzee vibes, but I really didn't enjoy this one.

[Rating: 4/10] Random die rolls and you get too many dead actions.  Theme of moonshining never came through at all

[Rating: 4/10] Feels like it plays itself with fairly obvious choices to make on most turns. It's not engaging to play.

[Rating: 4/10] Played on BGA.  Interesting mechanics of engine building, but little agency and quite frustrating card draw luck.

[Rating: 4/10] It looks really great, but offers very little in terms of gameplay. It wants to be an engine builder, but is too dependent on card luck and dice rolls. Especially at the beginning, many rounds are simply empty because you have bad luck with the dice, and even later on there is very little room for decision-making: in most rounds there is a clear best option.   In addition, the game is too lacking in interaction for what is ultimately a race. There are no opportunities to prevent my opponents from winning.  Overall, it's simply a very half-baked, almost unfinished, and unintuitive design.

[Rating: 4/10] Bien mais on reste un peu sur sa faim, un peu trop dépendant du hasard des cartes piochées malheureusement. Les illustrations sont belles!

[Rating: 5/10] Our game with 5p was not fun at all, game is long, dice color is not a elegant game design.
